title: Hierarchical Network Design: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Picture a big corporate office tower. Every floor has a different job. Networks are built the same way.

lines.t: A network is built the same way

scenes.heading: The office building
scenes.narration: A tidy network has three layers. The access layer is the floors where staff plug in. The distribution layer is the middle management who set the rules. The core layer is the lobby, moving people as fast as it can. Small buildings can merge the top two into a collapsed core.

scenes.heading: Where things go
scenes.narration: Keep the roles separate. The distribution layer applies policy, and the core just moves traffic. So ACLs live in distribution, never in the core. Small sites can merge them into one layer.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. Don't put A C Ls in the core. Access switches are normally layer two. And a two tier design is perfectly valid for small networks.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva hierarchical design lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Access, distribution and core. Keep policy in distribution, and speed in the core. Small sites can use a collapsed core. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva hierarchical design lab.
